belief: Everyone else's life is better than mine.
origins: Social media shows other people’s best moments: vacations, new homes, engagements, promotions, happy kids. We compare those highlights to our own full, ordinary days. The longer we scroll, the more our life seems lacking, and envy and discouragement grow.
teaches: Solomon observed, “All labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.” Proverbs says, “A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.” Paul writes, “Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else,” and “Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.” He also says, “I have learned to be content” in plenty and in need. Comparison steals contentment. Gratitude and honest self-examination restore it.
self_statements: Everyone else is happier than I am.
My life is boring and small.
What is wrong with my life?
errors: Comparing my whole life with others’ highlights.
Believing others’ lives are perfect and mine is not.
Overlooking blessings in my own life.
questions: What am I actually seeing online, and what am I not seeing?
How do I feel after scrolling?
What good things do I have that do not show up in photos?
What would I think of my life if I could not compare?
What does Scripture say about envy and contentment?
What limits on social media would help?
truth: Online lives are curated. My life has real struggles and real blessings, and God has given me my own path. I can limit comparison, give thanks, and invest in the life in front of me.
hw_truths: I do not see the whole picture online.
Envy rots; a tranquil heart gives life.
I can test my own work and not compare.
I can limit what feeds comparison.
log: Each day, write three things you are thankful for in your own life.
actions: Note your mood before and after scrolling.
Reduce time or unfollow accounts that trigger comparison.
Name ten blessings that do not appear on screen.
Connect with a friend face to face.
prayer: Lord, I compare my life to highlights and feel small. Teach me contentment, show me my own blessings, and help me live fully in the life You gave me. Amen.
hw_questions: What am I not seeing online?
How do I feel after scrolling?
Who can I see in person?
